   483: def _apply_article_duplicate_url_guard(
   484:     hits: List[Dict[str, Any]],
   485: ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   486:     """
   487:     Article-level duplicate URL guard.
   488: 
   489:     For a URL claimed by multiple phrases in the same article, keeps the
   490:     strongest phrase and MARKS the weaker ones as suppressed. It does NOT erase
   491:     their resolver evidence: best_target_url / resolved_targets are deliberately
   492:     left intact so the editor still sees what resolved, and the frontend is
   493:     responsible for honoring `duplicate_url_suppressed` when rendering links.
   494:     (Marking, not blanking — see inline note below.)
   495:     """

   500:         if not url:
   501:             continue

   508:             continue

   511:             key=lambda h: (
   512:                 float(h.get("best_target_runtime_score") or 0),
   513:                 float(h.get("score") or 0),
   514:             ),
   515:             reverse=True,
   516:         )

     1: """
     2: Highlight Selection Engine v2  (corrected)
     3: 
     4: ROLE (frozen):
     5:     The Smart Phrase Extractor is the single authority for phrase QUALITY.
     6:     This engine RANKS extractor-approved phrases and tags link opportunity.
     7:     It does NOT re-decide whether a phrase is "good".
     8: 
     9: What v2 does:
    10:     - extract candidates from the active phrase pool
    11:     - confirm the phrase physically occurs in the article (a fact, not a quality call)
    12:     - attach resolver/target signals as METADATA + ranking input (never a delete gate)
    13:     - tag each phrase  link_status = "linked" | "unlinked_opportunity"
    14:     - compute ONE normalized ranking score (extractor score is the base)
    15:     - sort, and emit EVERY article-present candidate
    16: 
    17: What v2 deliberately REMOVED (these were hidden phrase validators):
    18:     - weak_phrase_reason / WEAK_PHRASE_PATTERNS            (re-validation by regex)
    19:     - link_worthiness_score + suppress_low_link_worthiness (quality opinion)
    20:     - contextual_naturalness_score + suppression           (quality opinion)
    21:     - phrase_quality_score < 66 hard reject                (re-gating the authority)

    26: 
    27: Output contract:
    28:     candidates[]  -> every article-present, extractor-approved phrase, ranked,
    29:                      each carrying link_status and a family_root for the density
    30:                      engine. Nothing here is dropped for "quality".
    31:     rejected[]    -> only: empty phrase, exact duplicate, or not-present-in-article.
    32:

    34:     first_position / all_positions are offsets into the NORMALIZED article

     5:     The Smart Phrase Extractor is the single authority for phrase QUALITY.
     6:     This engine RANKS extractor-approved phrases and tags link opportunity.

MATCH LINE: 9
PATTERN: window_guard
CODE: ``candidate_window_guard``.
------------------------------------------------------------
     1: """
     2: Candidate window guard (corrected, niche-agnostic).
     3: 
     4: Role
     5: ----
     6: A *downstream* accept/reject gate. It receives an already-extracted candidate
     7: phrase and decides whether it is a clean anchor. It returns the same
     8: ``quality_gate`` record shape as before, so it is a drop-in replacement for
     9: ``candidate_window_guard``.
    10: 
    11: What changed vs. the previous version
    12: -------------------------------------
    13: The previous guard gated on large hand-curated *noun* vocabularies and a set of
    14: regexes memorised from specific documents. That made it (a) reject many perfectly
    15: good anchors whose modifier happened to be a common adjective ("simple interest",
    16: "regular expression", "search results"), (b) silently rewrite phrases to a
    17: hardcoded "core", and (c) carry a six-signal score that was decorative — every
    18: accepted phrase scored exactly 1.0, so the REVIEW band was unreachable.
    19: 
    20: This version follows the same asymmetry that makes phrase work universal:
    21: 
    22:   * VERBS are a (mostly) closed, niche-independent class -> we gate on a curated
    23:     *verb* lexicon (clause verbs, action-led leaks). Curating verbs is fine; they
    24:     do not vary by niche.
    25:   * NOUNS are open and vary by niche -> we NEVER reject a phrase because its head
    26:     noun is unknown. Weakness is judged on the HEAD, not on a modifier, and only
    27:     truly vacuous heads (thing/way/stuff/aspect) count.
    28: 
    29: The score is now honest: it is computed from real, transparent signals, so the
    30: ACCEPT / REVIEW / REJECT bands are all reachable and mean something.
    31: 
    32: POS layer
    33: ---------
    34: Verb-vs-noun and head decisions are driven by a part-of-speech tagger (NLTK when
    35: available, a light heuristic otherwise) rather than by guessing from word lists.
    36: Because taggers have a compound-noun bias on short fragments, the tagger is used
    37: as the primary signal and a small *closed verb class* backs it up: a token counts
    38: as a verb when the tagger says so AND we recognise it as a verb, or when it is a
    39: near-unambiguous verb (optimize, configure, affect...). Ambiguous noun homographs
    40: (build, drive, review, support, rate, plan...) are trusted as nouns, so
    41: "build quality", "product reviews" and "price increase" survive while
    42: "reduce churn" and "blood pressure improves" do not.
    43: 
    44: No required third-party or backend dependencies; NLTK and the learning hook are
    45: both optional and degrade gracefully.
    46: """

     1: from __future__ import annotations
     2: 
     3: from typing import Any, Dict
     4: 
     5: 
     6: def _to_float(value: Any, default: float = 0.0) -> float:
     7:     try:
     8:         return float(value)
     9:     except Exception:
    10:         return default
    11: 
    12: 
    13: def calibrate_resolver_score_v1(
    14:     *,
    15:     target_score: Any,
    16:     resolver_confidence: Any = None,
    17:     auto_floor: float = 0.70,
    18:     suggest_floor: float = 0.45,
    19: ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    20: 
    21:     raw_score = _to_float(target_score, 0.0)
    22: 
    23:     # Soft saturation curve:
    24:     # 300 = strong
    25:     # 600 = very strong
    26:     # Above 600 still approaches 1.0 but does not explode.
    27:     normalized = raw_score / (raw_score + 120.0) if raw_score > 0 else 0.0
    28:     normalized = max(0.0, min(1.0, normalized))
    29: 
    30:     existing_confidence = _to_float(resolver_confidence, normalized)
    31: 
    32:     calibrated_confidence = max(normalized, min(1.0, existing_confidence))
    33: 
    34:     if calibrated_confidence >= 0.85:
    35:         band = "very_high"
    36:     elif calibrated_confidence >= auto_floor:
    37:         band = "high"
    38:     elif calibrated_confidence >= suggest_floor:
    39:         band = "medium"
    40:     elif calibrated_confidence > 0:
    41:         band = "low"
    42:     else:
    43:         band = "none"
    44: 
    45:     return {
    46:         "has_score_calibration": True,
    47:         "raw_score": round(raw_score, 4),
    48:         "normalized_score": round(normalized, 4),
    49:         "calibrated_confidence": round(calibrated_confidence, 4),
    50:         "confidence_band": band,

PATTERN: extract_smart_phrases
CODE: **no required dependencies**. ``extract_smart_phrases(...)`` keeps the same
------------------------------------------------------------
    15: away. It also over-trimmed adjectival ``-ly`` modifiers ("weekly report",
    16: "monthly budget") and rejected its own verb-bearing intent phrases
    17: ("how to calculate ...").
    18: 
    19: This version fixes the asymmetry that makes an extractor universal:
    20: 
    21:   * VERBS are a (mostly) closed, niche-independent class -> we keep a broad
    22:     verb lexicon and gate structurally on it.
    23:   * NOUNS are open and vary by niche -> we never require a head to be in a
    24:     curated list. When a POS tagger is available we *trust its tag* for the
    25:     head; otherwise an unknown content word defaults to a valid head.

MATCH LINE: 27

CODE: The public function `extract_smart_phrases(...)` keeps the same signature and
------------------------------------------------------------
    10: The old extractor slid fixed 2/3/4-word windows across a token stream and then
    11: tried to *reject* the bad ones with several hundred hand-written blocklists and
    12: regexes. Sliding windows inherently slice through the middle of grammatical
    13: constituents, so "calculate the fertile window" becomes "calculate the",
    14: "the fertile", "fertile window", etc. The blocklists can never enumerate every
    15: truncation, so fragments leak through.
    16: 
    17: This version flips the approach: instead of cutting arbitrary windows and
    18: filtering, it (1) chunks each sentence into whole noun-phrase / verb-object
    19: constituents, then (2) trims both ends down to content-word boundaries and
    20: rejects anything that still starts or ends on a function word. A phrase is kept
    21: only if it begins and ends on a content word and ends on a noun-like head. That
    22: single structural rule removes essentially all "hanging" output.
    23: 
    24: It prefers spaCy or NLTK if installed (best accuracy) and otherwise falls back
    25: to a self-contained heuristic chunker, so it has **no required dependencies**.
    26: 
    27: The public function `extract_smart_phrases(...)` keeps the same signature and
    28: output shape as before, so this is a drop-in replacement.
    29: """

   194: 
   195: def _phrase_candidates(item: Dict[str, Any]) -> Set[str]:
   196:     """
   197:     Universal canonical phrase extractor for topic clustering.
   198:     Uses titles/slugs to produce stable 2-3 word topic phrases.
   199:     Avoids sliding-window loops like "sleep regression sleep".
   200:     """
   201:     raw_parts: List[str] = []
   202: 
   203:     for k in ("title", "h1", "label"):
   204:         val = str(item.get(k) or "").strip()
   205:         if val:
   206:             raw_parts.append(val)
   207: 
   208:     path = str(item.get("path") or "")
   209:     if path:
   210:         raw_parts.append(path.replace("/", " ").replace("-", " ").replace("_", " "))
   211: 
   212:     for k in ("matched_phrases", "aliases"):
   213:         vals = item.get(k) or []
   214:         if isinstance(vals, list):
   215:             raw_parts.extend(str(v or "") for v in vals if str(v or "").strip())
   216: 
   217:     out: Set[str] = set()
   218: 
   219:     for raw in raw_parts:
   220:         clean = re.sub(r"\.aspx\b", " ", str(raw), flags=re.I)
   221:         clean = re.sub(r"\b\d+\b", " ", clean)
   222:         toks = _dedupe_consecutive_tokens(_tokens(clean))
   223: 
   224:         if len(toks) < 2:
   225:             continue
   226: 
   227:         # Prefer first meaningful 2-word and 3-word title phrases.
   228:         for n in (2, 3):
   229:             if len(toks) >= n:
   230:                 phrase = " ".join(toks[:n]).strip()
   231:                 if not _is_bad_phrase_label(phrase):
   232:                     out.add(phrase)

     1: // Lightweight loader + resolver for Entity Map (fallbacks-only friendly)
     2: export async function loadEntityMap() {
     3:   const res = await fetch("/assets/data/entity_map.json", { cache: "no-store" });
     4:   const raw = await res.json();
     5:   return buildIndex(raw);
     6: }
     7: 
     8: function buildIndex(entities) {
     9:   const byId = new Map();
    10:   const aliasToId = new Map();
    11:   const regexes = []; // [{re: RegExp, id}]
    12: 
    13:   for (const e of entities) {
    14:     byId.set(e.id, e);
    15:     (e.aliases || []).forEach(a => aliasToId.set(String(a||"").toLowerCase(), e.id));
    16:     (e.patterns || []).forEach(p => { try { regexes.push({ re: new RegExp(p, "i"), id: e.id }); } catch {} });
    17:   }
    18:   return { byId, aliasToId, regexes };
    19: }
    20: 
    21: export function resolveEntity(text, idx) {
    22:   if (!idx || !text) return null;
    23:   const t = String(text).toLowerCase().trim();
    24:   const id1 = idx.aliasToId.get(t);
    25:   if (id1) return idx.byId.get(id1);
    26:   for (const { re, id } of idx.regexes) { try { if (re.test(text)) return idx.byId.get(id); } catch {} }
    27:   return null;
    28: }
    29:

    31:   return entity?.internal?.url
